key_insight: On-Policy Context Distillation (OPCD) trains a student LM on its own generated trajectories while minimizing reverse KL against a context-conditioned teacher, enabling the student to internalize in‑context knowledge into its parameters.
problem_solved: Reduces reliance on long in-context prompts by converting transient in-context knowledge into model parameters, improving efficiency and robustness of language models when using or deploying contextual knowledge.
method: On-policy generation: the student model produces its own trajectories (responses) conditioned on contexts.

Reverse KL distillation: optimize the student to minimize reverse Kullback–Leibler divergence to a context-conditioned teacher distribution, aligning student outputs with teacher behavior while preserving mode-seeking properties.
Bridging paradigms: combine on-policy distillation techniques with context distillation to internalize experiential/in-context knowledge into model weights.
impact: OPCD helps LMs learn and retain context-specific information within their parameters, lowering inference-time prompting costs and improving downstream performance for tasks that rely on ephemeral or experiential knowledge.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: teacher (context-conditioned) → loss (reverse KL) ← student, with student generating trajectories looped back to training.
Before/After graphic: long prompt usage vs. compact model with internalized context (showing reduced prompt length or latency).
Bar/line chart: performance or calibration gains across tasks (e.g., experiential knowledge) comparing baseline, standard distillation, and OPCD.
Icon set: 'memory' chip for internalized knowledge, 'loop' for on-policy training, and 'KL' symbol for the loss objective.
paper_title: On-Policy Context Distillation for Language Models
paper_authors: Tianzhu Ye, Li Dong, Xun Wu, Shaohan Huang, Furu Wei
